blocks.html: humanity is broadly unsatisfied in its current state and the continued progression of ai development will only worsen a deepening crisis.
reckoning with an uncertain future has never been an easy thing. read: anthropic’s projections for the economy.

without ethical guidelines defining responsible development, i find it quite hard to see a world where people live happy lives anymore. a lot of this comes from my own life. intrinsically, i think people have stopped doing things for the right reasons, and it will be very hard to get this out of people.

the idea of doing things for telic vs atelic purposes is extraordinarily appealing to me especially in a time where i find myself increasingly uncertain of what my life will look like in the next five, ten, or even two years. everyone should read the og book on telic vs atelic (setiya i think?)

on one hand, there is a narrative that the world is a cruel place — you need to do things to survive, even if it goes against the code of doing things for true fulfillment (meaning doing things purely for atelic purposes). this is not an illogical argument. the world will die trying to bend itself to everyone’s will. one must do what they have to do to survive. but it begs the question: are you truly living if every day consists of doing something that kills you just to ‘live’ on someone else’s terms???

i truly believe that this narrative is the exact reason why humanity will never be happy. we’ve devolved into this vicious cycle of doing things purely for telic purposes, lacking any meaning or significance in our life. man is on the perpetual hedonic treadmill, and as long as this accelerated industrialization continues, i don’t think we will ever recover.

i do think there is an alternative narrative to consider, though. we talk a lot about agi and what it means for jobs and work, but for a moment consider a utopia where agi has solved physical labor. let’s say agi solves software (we are not far from this). let’s say agi solves 80–85% of our jobs (in a very optimistic situation). is there any value left in our work then? what is our purpose? do we go back to being custodians of the earth? what is the meaning of money? does it matter? how will people react?

will we actually become happier? i think this is the trillion dollar gamble no one has considered. truly, i can see it going either way. i think if ai development finally peaks and plateaus at agi and we’ve reached a complete post-agi world where the majority of people don’t have to work anymore, we will face equal numbers of depressed and equal numbers of happy. billions will be happy to finally pursue the things they love. but an equal amount, in my opinion, will be consumed with the sheer shock of the fact that their whole life amounted to (in their eyes) nothing. this is a soul crushing reality billions will face.

without money, without the force of industrialization bearing down on the billions of working men and women, what will come of them? will this lack of attachment to anything be better for us? only time can tell. buddha had his own thoughts on this…

i don’t know how i feel about this at all. a lot of this is unhashed thoughts, mostly just kept to myself. but as someone who has grappled with this question of doing fulfilling things with their life, the truth is the future scares me a lot. it could just be a fear of the uncertain — something many struggle with.
tldr; very interested in seeing how the next decade plays out. scared for myself, but how we build in the next 4–5 years could dramatically shape human sociology and behavior for centuries.
